riskFindings: The signed challenge is stateless and reusable by the same subject for 15 minutes; it is not atomically consumed, so old proof can replay after a newer link.

Wallet proof payloads reuse RELAY_SECRET with application authentication, internal order-access proofs and wallet-send markers; no dedicated wallet-proof signing and rotation domain was observed, so compromise or rotation has cross-purpose blast radius.
Sensitive TON verify and disconnect routes accept the default up-to-24-hour Telegram initData bearer without a fresh-action challenge or step-up.
Both API proof-verification routes ignore wallet_link.remember returning false and may report verified=true when durable persistence failed.
Disconnect maps repository failure to removed=0, always returns ok=true, and the Mini App ignores response truth.
The primary-key upsert blindly replaces the current address for a chain without version/CAS, proof digest, prior-link evidence or monotonic epoch.
Disconnect hard-deletes the link without a minimal revocation receipt, audit correlation, retention policy or backup-expiry evidence.
wallet_link catches read failures and returns an empty list, misreporting database outage as not connected.
No route-specific challenge/proof/link/disconnect throttling or explicit request-body size/depth bound was observed before chain public-key lookup.
The generic proof-message GET places the public address in the query string, increasing proxy/access-log privacy exposure.
Raw Telegram user IDs are logged for proof verification, full addresses/balances/history are rendered, and no classification/retention/deletion evidence accompanies the link table.

The deployed wallet store differs from checkout and retains SQLite runtime CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS paths; current PostgreSQL selection makes that path dormant but artifact drift remains unresolved.
The observed production table has zero links, so repository/route presence cannot prove any authenticated production lifecycle.
